overview: The SBA's Surety Bond Program guarantees bonds for small contractors, which are financial guarantees that a project will be completed, making it easier for small businesses to win government and private construction jobs. This bill nearly triples the largest contract the program normally covers, from $6.5 million to $18 million. That limit would temporarily drop by a third in any year the SBA asks Congress for extra money for the program's fund, until the fund is again covering its own costs. The SBA could spend up to 2 percent of the fund each year on running the program, and would have to send Congress an annual report on guarantees, claims paid and the fund's financial health. The Government Accountability Office, Congress's watchdog, would also review how the SBA approves applicants. As of May 4, 2026, it had passed the Senate and was being held at the desk in the House.
for: Supporters say the old limit has not kept up with construction costs, and raising it lets more small contractors compete for larger projects, while the new reports keep the fund accountable.
against: Critics say guaranteeing much larger bonds raises the government's potential losses if contractors default, and allowing administrative costs to come out of the fund could strain it.
